strings.name: Janet Yellen
strings.role: Economist · Former Fed chair and Treasury secretary
strings.summary: Janet Yellen moved from research on unemployment and macroeconomics into public policymaking. She led the San Francisco Fed, the Federal Reserve and the US Treasury, becoming the first woman to hold the latter two offices. Her public career spanned the post-crisis recovery and post-pandemic inflation, linking employment, price stability and international coordination. She also acknowledged underestimating inflation, illustrating the uncertainty surrounding economic decisions.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 13 November 2026; selected events reach a September 2026 public conversation. Her Treasury service ended in 2025. Leadership milestones and the inflation forecasting error are both included; economic outcomes are not attributed to one person.
strings.influence.rationale: Led the Federal Reserve and the US Treasury, exercising international influence through labor-economics research and macroeconomic policy.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: BA in economics, Brown University (1967); PhD in economics, Yale University (1971)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Breaking leadership barriers
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Became the first woman to chair the Federal Reserve and lead the US Treasury, having also chaired the Council of Economic Advisers.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Connecting labor research and policy
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Studied the causes and effects of unemployment through a career spanning universities, central banking and fiscal policymaking.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Discusses policy and leadership
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Berkeley Haas released an extended conversation reviewing her path from university teaching to public service in Washington.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Ends her Treasury service
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Returned to research at Brookings after leaving the Treasury; her service had run from 2021 to 2025.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Acknowledges an inflation forecasting error
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Said in an interview that her earlier judgment about inflation had been wrong and supported Fed action to curb rising prices.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Sworn in as Treasury secretary
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Became the first woman to hold the office, bringing central-banking experience to pandemic-era economic policy.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Becomes Federal Reserve chair
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Succeeded Bernanke as the first woman to lead the Fed and served until February 2018.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Becomes Fed vice chair
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Moved from the San Francisco Fed to the Board’s vice chairmanship during the post-crisis recovery.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Leads the San Francisco Fed
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Became president and CEO of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco and served until 2010.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Chairs the Council of Economic Advisers
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Left the Fed Board to chair the White House Council of Economic Advisers until 1999.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Joins UC Berkeley
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Joined Berkeley after work at Harvard, the Fed and the London School of Economics, combining unemployment research with teaching.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Earns a Yale doctorate
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Completed her economics PhD and began teaching at Harvard, developing a career in macroeconomics.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Graduates from Brown
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Earned an economics degree with highest honors before entering graduate study at Yale.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Brooklyn
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born and raised in Brooklyn, New York, and later focused her research on employment and macroeconomics.
